blocks.text: São Paulo: trees, pedestrians, and cars beside the city’s high-rises

Meet your English-speaking guide for a driving tour of historic and modern São Paulo.

In the historic centre, the tour takes in Praça da Sé, the cathedral, the Japanese quarter, the square where the city was founded, the Viaduto do Chá, the Municipal Theatre for opera and ballet, the square by the station, the suburban railway station, the Municipal Market, Praça da República, and the Terraço Itália building.

Then see Paulista Avenue and Ibirapuera Park. The park has lakes, canals, spreading trees, sports courts, and bike paths. It is also home to the obelisk commemorating the heroes of the 1932 Revolution and the Monumento às Bandeiras, dedicated to expeditions that travelled into the interior in search of gold and precious stones. The tour ends with a look at upscale neighbourhoods, contemporary architecture, and a district known for its graffiti.

Transfer to the airport for your flight to Iguazú, then transfer to the hotel. Afterwards, visit the Brazilian side of the falls.

Iguazú Falls lies in a national park surrounded by tropical forest. The falls are thought to have formed through volcanic activity and shifts in the earth’s crust. The name Iguazú means “big water” in Guaraní. The river splits into 275 waterfalls, and the trail follows the cascades to the Devil’s Throat. From the viewpoints, you can see individual streams, the canyon, clouds of spray, and rainbows over the water.
